In a modeled EV battery design, what happens when an individual cell becomes weak?

A. The battery pack stops using the remaining cells
B. The weak cell is bypassed so the rest can keep operating
C. The weak cell is automatically replaced while driving
D. The pack switches to a larger battery
E. The vehicle charges the weak cell at a higher voltage

Choose before seeing how the crowd answered — then follow your choice through the Cosmos Butterfly.

discovery.title: Could one weak battery cell stop retiring an entire EV pack?
discovery.summary: Chalmers researchers modeled an EV battery architecture that can bypass degraded cells, extending pack life by more than 20% under some conditions. The approach is not yet in production vehicles.
discovery.why_it_matters: Longer-lasting packs could reduce replacement costs, material demand and battery waste, but the reported gain is model-based rather than a demonstrated fleet outcome.

discovery.title: Antarctic sea ice is hitting record-low daily levels unusually early
discovery.summary: NSIDC's October 7 analysis says Antarctic sea ice extent fell sharply after its September maximum and reached record-low daily extents from October 2 onward.
discovery.why_it_matters: Sea-ice changes affect polar ecosystems and the exchange of heat between ocean and atmosphere; the longer-term implications require continued observation and attribution.

discovery.title: Can a graphene wrapper help fuel-cell platinum last longer?
discovery.summary: Nagoya University researchers report a nitrogen-containing graphene coating around platinum nanoparticles that retained 96.9% of active surface after 30,000 durability cycles, according to a research-news roundup.
discovery.why_it_matters: If the result translates beyond laboratory testing, longer-lived catalysts could reduce a key material constraint in fuel cells. Commercial performance remains unproven.

discovery.title: Can a collar help reveal how wildfire smoke affects wildlife?
discovery.summary: Colorado State researchers announced an affordable, open-source air-quality monitor designed to track particulate exposure on wildlife collars and connect smoke levels with animal behavior.
discovery.why_it_matters: Better exposure data could improve understanding of wildfire impacts on animals and potentially inform smoke-health monitoring more broadly.
